title: Total Sum of Interaction Cost in Tree Groups
summary: Given an integer n and an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array edges, and an integer array group indicating group labels for each node, calculate the total interaction cost for all unordered pairs (u, v) where u and v are in the same group.
statement: Given an integer n and an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array edges, and an integer array group indicating group labels for each node, calculate the total interaction cost for all unordered pairs (u, v) where u and v are in the same group. The interaction cost between u and v is the number of edges on the unique path connecting them.
constraints: n is up to 100,000; edges is a valid tree and group has length n.
Each unordered same-group pair contributes its tree distance.
Return the total contribution over all groups.
hints: At a node, pairs whose lowest common ancestor is that node lie in different processed child maps or at the node itself.
Store per group both node count and sum of depths, merging smaller maps into the largest.
For two same-group sets, sum distance as countA·depthSumB + countB·depthSumA - 2·depthLCA·countA·countB.
Every same-group pair is counted exactly once when its two sides first meet at its lowest common ancestor.
editorial: Every same-group pair is counted exactly once when its two sides first meet at its lowest common ancestor.

tests.explanation: The three pair distances are one, one, and two, totaling four.
Six leaf/center or leaf/leaf pairs have total distance nine.
